headlines.title: ‘Very special moment': Parents, first responders recount baby's delivery in SF traffic jam
headlines.description: It was a perfectly normal delivery in the most abnormal place possible: bumper-to-bumper traffic in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. When Karollyn Zepeda realized Saturday afternoon that it was time to head to the hospital to deliver her child, she and her partner Nate Geminiano didn’t expect traffic to derail their birth plan. “I had looked at Nate and I was like, ‘You know what, I’m scared I’m gonna have this baby right here,’ especially because just as we were leaving my house my water did break,” Zepeda said. With traffic on Crossover Drive through Golden Gate Park at a standstill, Geminiano pulled over, called 911 and started asking other people stuck in traffic for help. “I told them that she was in labor,” Geminiano said. “Then they assisted me in just going around to other cars trying to find any medical professionals.” Katie Higgins, a trained doula, was sitting in traffic several cars away when she heard those calls for help. She jumped into action, along with other helpers. “Someone was going through their car and ultimately found a box of gloves that were very important and helpful,” Higgins said. “A couple women showed up with a big blanket to give her privacy. Everybody, all these San Franciscans came together.” Zepeda said she felt relief as soon as Higgins showed up. “She immediately, I think, said to me, ‘I’ve done two home births. I’m a doula.’ And I was like, ‘Oh, thank God.’ I was just immediately relived,” Zepeda said. The gridlock also delayed first responders. Both the American Medical Response (AMR) ambulance crew and the San Francisco firefighter team that were dispatched to the scene realized they were not going to be able to make it to the call in their vehicles, so they had to hike. Brian Ingram with AMR tried pushing a gurney through traffic before settling on another plan. “I asked one of the firefighters, ‘I just need one person. Just grab the front. We just got to try to make it up this dirt hill,'” he said. When first responders eventually arrived, they all pitched in to help. A few pushes later, a new child was born. “Being able to grab that baby, I wrapped her up in a blanket and turned around and handed her to dad,” firefighter William Melton said. “It was a very special moment.”

headlines.title: Vallejo woman awarded Carnegie Medal for heroism
headlines.description: A Vallejo woman has earned the highest civilian award for heroism for jumping into action to save a stranger’s life. Amanda Williams is one of 16 people in the United States and Canada being presented with the Carnegie Medal for heroism. “It’s pretty surreal,” Williams said. “I don’t think it’s hit me yet.” Williams helped save Roscell Wallace, a 29-year-old man who was attacked by a knife-wielding relative last year. “He was yelling, ‘Help me! He’s trying to kill me!” Williams recalled. “He just kept saying that over and over. ‘He’s trying to kill me! He’s trying to kill me!” Williams, a single mom and DoorDash driver, happened to be driving by the scene of the knife attack and instinctively jumped out to help. “I grabbed his wrist – the one that held the knives – I grabbed his wrist so he couldn’t swing at him anymore,” Williams said. Williams then managed to wrestle two knives from the attacker’s hand. “I didn’t really think about it,” Williams said. “It was either I had to do something or he was going to die. It was a split second. You don’t really have a chance to think about it. It’s either you do something or you don’t.” The attacker, Henry Johnson, stole Williams’ car and totaled it before getting arrested. Johnson is set to go to trial on attempted murder and other charges. Roscell said he’s forever grateful to Williams for stepping in to help. “She’s like an angel,” Roscell said. “God sent her to save me.”

headlines.title: NorCal Rumble unveiled as new name for Bay Area women's volleyball team
headlines.description: A new Major League Volleyball team in the Bay Area now has a name: NorCal Rumble. The team announced its name on Tuesday and will begin playing at Tech CU Arena in San Jose in 2027. Kerri Walsh Jennings, a Bay Area native and three-time Olympic gold medalist, is one of the team owners. The volleyball legend and NorCal Rumble President Heather Vaughan joined NBC Bay Area to discuss the team’s new logo, the league and why it is important for the region to have a professional women’s volleyball team. headlines.title: Death of woman in Brentwood police custody was caused by a stroke, DA says
headlines.description: The Contra Costa County District Attorney’s Office said Tuesday that the 2025 death of a woman one week after her arrest by Brentwood police was caused by a stroke and not by police restraint, ending a year-long investigation into her death. “While incredibly tragic, Yolanda Ramirez died from a stroke and other health-related issues, as opposed to police use of force,” the District Attorney’s Office wrote in a report. “No further action will be taken in this case.” The decision means prosecutors will not seek charges against Brentwood police officers Aaron Peachman and Danielle Tjhia, who detained Ramirez, 72, outside a home in Brentwood on Sept. 26, 2025. Ramirez was found barely conscious and confused in the back of their patrol car 20 minutes after her arrest following an altercation with her sister over the well-being of their brother, an elderly man who suffers from dementia-like symptoms. Ramirez was then taken to a hospital, where she died on Oct. 3, 2025, according to the district attorney’s report. Brentwood Jul 16 Brentwood Feb 27 Brentwood Jan 1 Melissa Nold, an attorney representing the Ramirez family, said that Contra Costa County District Attorney Diana Becton made the wrong call in the finding of death due to natural causes. “This is after her office failed to investigate the case at all until there was public pressure, a second autopsy and I had investigated,” Nold wrote in a social media post. After Ramirez tried to leave the scene when police arrived, body camera footage from both officers showed Ramirez was forcibly put into handcuffs and put into the back of the car, where she was left alone for 20 minutes after allegedly hitting her head on the outside of the car during her arrest. Camera footage from the patrol car showed Ramirez, who was diabetic, slumped in the backseat and unresponsive when officers returned. She was later sent to a hospital, where she died. A Contra Costa County coroner’s autopsy immediately following Ramirez’s death found that she died from a stroke and did not have any bruising on her head, ultimately ruling her death was due to natural causes. A second autopsy ordered by Ramirez’s family differed, concluding that Ramirez had suffered “blunt force trauma to the head” from contact with police and that her death was a homicide. A coroner’s inquest into Ramirez’s death in July ended in a split verdict by a jury, with seven jurors ruling her death was from natural causes and eight ruling her death was an accident. An inquest is a process separate from a medical examiner’s probe into an in-custody death and is when a jury reviews witness testimony and determines the manner of the cause of an individual’s death. Jurors were advised to choose between four possible rulings: accident, suicide, natural causes and “at the hands of another person, other than by accident.”

headlines.title: 19-year-old College of San Mateo football player killed in crash
headlines.description: The College of San Mateo is mourning the loss of a student-athlete. Ja’Marion “Pop” Grace, a 19-year-old freshman defensive back on the school’s football team, was killed in a car crash last weekend. Two of his teammates were also injured. “Pop wasn’t just a teammate – he was a brother,” the College of San Mateo football team wrote in a post on social media. “He lit up every room he walked into with his infectious energy and smile, he had a way of making everyone around him feel special. Whether he was dancing in the locker room, cracking jokes in team meetings, or showing up for his teammates off the field, Pop gave everything he had each and every day.” College officials did not say when or where the crash happened. The California Highway Patrol reported a deadly crash Sunday morning on Highway 101 near Yerba Buena Road in San Jose. The CHP said a preliminary investigation indicates the driver of a 2013 Ford Fusion lost control of the vehicle while traveling northbound. A 19-year-old passenger from Fairfield was ejected from the vehicle and died from his injuries. headlines.title: ‘Unprecedented corruption': SF sues Trump's Truth Social over paid subscriptions
headlines.description: President Donald Trump’s Truth Social is accused of “unprecedented corruption” and insider trading, according to a lawsuit announced Tuesday. San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu announced the lawsuit against the platform’s parent company, Trump Media, for selling subscriptions allowing early access to the president’s social posts. Chiu said the paid access violates federal ethics laws and facilitates insider trading. “Trump Media created a marketplace that enables insider trading, which Trump directly profits from,” Chiu said in a statement. “This scheme turns the public trust into private profit. It is corruption, plain and simple. Californians should not be forced to compete against wealthy trading firms buying early access to market‑moving information. We are acting decisively to stop this corruption and protect Californians, who work hard, save, and invest responsibly. They deserve a fair marketplace and an ethical government that won’t sell them out to make a quick profit.” Truth Social over the summer started selling a subscription that allows financial firms and other organizations to get alerts for new posts made by Trump and other top accounts before general users do. For a high-frequency trading firm, even milliseconds of a head start could make a huge difference, NBC News recently reported. The lawsuit, which aims to stop the service, claims the deal is making Truth Social an estimated $60,000 to $100,000 a month and violates California’s unfair competition law. Trump Media is responding to the lawsuit by saying its service is no different than any standard subscription uses pay for ways to trade stock successfully. Trump has the largest following on the platform and has used Truth Social as his go-to platform to release official statements throughout his second term. NBC News contributed to this report. headlines.title: Uber driver arrested for alleged sexual assault of teen boy in San Jose
headlines.description: A ride-hailing driver was arrested earlier this month for allegedly sexually assaulting a teen boy during a trip in San Jose, police announced Tuesday. The teen was heading to downtown San Jose in an Uber on the evening of Sept. 12 when the driver, identified as 32-year-old Foster City resident Anuj Kumar, allegedly sexually assaulted him, police said. According to court records, Kumar inappropriately touched the 14-year-old boy and engaged the child locks on the vehicle to prevent him from leaving. Investigators said the sexual assault happened just outside the teen’s destination: the Hammer Theatre near San Jose State University. “I know it happened inside the car, and after the survivor got out of the vehicle he did the right thing by contacting SJPD,” police spokesperson Stacie Shih said. “We’re fortunate that the victim reported this to the San Jose Police Department immediately so that we could begin our investigation.” Authorities utilized automated license plate reader cameras to identify the suspect vehicle and subsequently Kumar as the suspect. He was arrested on Sept. 13 in Foster City and booked into jail for sexual assault of a minor, according to police. In a statement, an Uber spokesperson said, “What’s been reported is deeply disturbing and has no place on our platform. We take reports of sexual assault extremely serious, and the driver has been permanently banned from the Uber platform. Our team is supporting law enforcement with their investigation.” Kumar had been an Uber driver for two and a half years and had a 4.95 rating, according to court records. Detectives believe there may be additional victims. Anyone with information about the case or similar cases is encouraged to contact San Jose police Detective Hoang by email at 4684@sanjoseca.gov or by phone at 408-277-4102. headlines.title: Discovery of golden mussels at Lake Del Valle prompts quarantine on boats
headlines.description: Invasive golden mussels have been found at Lake Del Valle near Livermore, prompting park officials to enforce a 30-day quarantine on watercraft. The 5-mile-long lake at Del Valle Regional Park is part of the East Bay Regional Park District. Until this week, Contra Loma Reservoir in Antioch was the only waterbody in the district where golden mussels had been found, officials said Monday. Now, boaters at Lake Del Valle are under the same rules governing Contra Loma: a 30-day quarantine before watercraft that have been on the lake are permitted at any other waterbody managed by the district. Golden mussels originated in Asia and quickly spread through the state since first being identified in the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta in 2024. The mussel is a freshwater species that inhabits shallow waters and hard surfaces, impeding water flow, clogging pipes and damaging equipment while also affecting native species. California has emphasized a “Clean, Drain, Dry” campaign for local boaters to try to stop the spread of mussels or other invasive species. Park district staff have used tamper-proof bands placed between the watercraft and trailer when a boat leaves the lake. These bands serve as proof that the vessel hadn’t launched in other waters. Boats that launch exclusively at Lake Del Valle and return with an intact Del Valle boat band will not be subject to the quarantine. The park district has used the lake-specific bands since summer 2025 in an effort to prevent the introduction of golden mussels. Boats without a park district boat band are subject to inspection for the presence of quagga, zebra, and golden mussels. Inspection fees are $10 for motorized vessels and $5 for car-top watercraft and inflatables. Fees partially offset the cost of the inspection program. Other agencies that manage waterbodies elsewhere in the Bay Area and beyond may impose their own quarantine requirements, so boaters should check the websites of respective managing agencies for current rules. More information is available at ebparks.org/mussels.

headlines.title: Man arrested in connection with 2 homicides in San Jose
headlines.description: A man was arrested in connection with two homicides in San Jose after he allegedly flagged down a police officer and said he had committed a homicide, according to authorities. The investigation began around 5:14 p.m. Saturday when a San Jose police patrol officer was flagged down by a man who alleged he had committed a homicide. Officers responded to the area of Lelong and Alma avenues, where they found a man dead, police said. The suspect, identified by police as Marcelino Castro, 28, of San Jose, was taken into custody. During the investigation, Castro provided detectives with information about a second homicide in the area of Autumn Parkway and Coleman Avenue, according to police. Detectives responded to that location and found a second person dead. Castro was arrested and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on two counts of murder. Police said the motive and circumstances surrounding the deaths remain under investigation. The deaths are being investigated as San Jose’s 20th and 21st homicides of 2026. Anyone with information is asked to contact Detective Sgt. Van Den Broeck at 3829@sanjoseca.gov or Detective Estantino at 4339@sanjoseca.gov. The San Jose Police Department’s Homicide Unit can also be reached at 408-277-5283.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot and descriptions from the secretary of state: Proposition 1: Authorizes bonds for housing affordability programs Proposition 2: Increases state’s rainy day fund Proposition 3: Provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending existing tax on high incomes Proposition 4: Repeals prohibition against public funding of election campaigns. Proposition 5: Changes recall election process for statewide officers. Proposition 37: Creates loan program for middle-income buyers of qualified new homes. Proposition 38: Authorizes bonds for immunology medical research. Proposition 39: Prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification. Proposition 40: Imposes one-time tax on certain taxpayers. Proposition 41: Prohibits new state taxes that exclude revenues from state spending limit. Requires audits for new state special taxes. Proposition 42: Prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive state taxes. Proposition 43: Limits voters’ ability to raise revenues for local government services. Proposition 44: Requires community health clinics spend 90% of revenue on program services. Proposition 45: Modifies environmental review for certain projects. Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026: Events, schedules, what to know
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again. San Francisco Fleet Week is back. The fall tradition will be highlighted by the Blue Angels screaming across the skies, but there are plenty of other events to experience. Check out the guide below to learn more about Fleet Week events. What is San Francisco Fleet Week? San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual celebration of the nation’s sea services. A multi-day air show, parade of ships and ship tours highlight the weeklong festivities. “San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual public event that honors the contributions of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces while advancing cooperation and knowledge among civilian- and military-based Humanitarian Assistance personnel,” a statement on the event’s website reads. When is San Francisco Fleet Week 2026? Fleet Week is scheduled to take place Sunday, Oct. 4 through Monday, Oct. 12. San Francisco Fleet Week Air Show Head to a location along San Francisco Bay between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz to catch a thrilling aerial show featuring the Blue Angels, a United Airlines 777, and much more. When: 12 p.m. – 4 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 9, Saturday, Oct. 10 and Sunday, Oct. 11 Lineup and schedule: Stay tuned for detailed information on the airshow lineup and schedule Where: Ticketed seating located at the Marina Green in San Francisco Tickets: Air show tickets are available via the San Francisco Fleet Week website Note: Gates open at 10 a.m. on Friday and 11 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday Bay Area Jan 16 San Francisco Sep 3 San Francisco Fleet Week Parade of Ships Set your eyes on the water near the Golden Gate Bridge to catch the fleet of ships arriving in the Bay, escorted by a San Francisco Fire Department boat shooting water into the air. When: 11 a.m. – 12 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 9 Where: San Francisco Bay waterfront (the parade can be seen from locations along the water between the Golden Gate Bridge and the Bay Bridge) San Francisco Fleet Week Ship Tours Climb aboard various ships to see what it’s like to be a sailor in the U.S. Navy and U.S. Coast Guard. The visiting ships will be announced in late September. headlines.title: 34-foot La Catrina statue celebrates Día de los Muertos in Oakland
headlines.description: A towering symbol of Día de los Muertos is coming to Oakland’s Fruitvale Transit Village as the Bay Area celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month. A new La Catrina statue is being assembled at the transit village after arriving by truck from Mexico, where it was created by two artists. Once fully assembled, the statue will stand 34 feet tall. The artists believe it will be the tallest Catrina figure in the United States. La Catrina will face west overlooking the Fruitvale BART tracks. The Unity Council, the community development corporation that built the Fruitvale Transit Village, commissioned the artwork to celebrate Día de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead, on Nov. 1. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.
